statement: A naive hard character-count truncation at exactly 60 chars is NOT conformant for the new (question-derived) slug scheme -- it must be rejected even though it is what a byte-for-byte port of a generic slugify() would produce.
input_text: One reviewed taxonomy document mapping existing error classes and their owners
reason: A plain 60-character hard cut lands mid-word, splitting 'classes' into 'classe'. The conformant slugify() finds the last '-' inside the 60-char window and cuts there instead, yielding 'one-reviewed-taxonomy-document-mapping-existing-error' (55 chars). NOTE: the pre-existing LEGACY slug function (used only to recognise old filenames, see FIL-003/FIL-004) intentionally reproduces this exact hard-cut behaviour and must never be changed to match -- this invalid example applies to the NEW-scheme slugify() only.
note: Verified: whyfile.passes.capture._legacy_slug() on this exact input DOES produce 'one-reviewed-taxonomy-document-mapping-existing-error-classe' (mid-word) by design -- that legacy behaviour is correct for ITS rule (FIL-004-adjacent: reproduce old filenames exactly); slugify() must not be 'simplified' to match it.
